APPROVED_OPERATIONAL_REQUIREMENTS: The clean system has case, endpoint, source, collection-plan, attempt, evidence-item, custody-event, and export identities with explicit ownership and stable references.
Collection plans distinguish authorized live endpoint sources from imported offline bundles and bind each requested source to policy, platform capability, limits, and case scope.

A source request has explicit lifecycle and truthful terminal dispositions for complete, partial, unavailable, rejected, cancelled, and failed work; coverage derives from requested sources and all dispositions.

Every evidence item retains source, case, endpoint, collection, attempt, capture-time, integrity, and custody provenance sufficient to distinguish repeated observations from conflicting identity reuse.
Events and results are accepted only under recorded source authority and active attempt; delayed, duplicate, conflicting, or superseded observations cannot silently regress accepted state.
The workflow is restartable: queue claims, leases, checkpoints, accepted result events, manifest publication, and export state have explicit durable ownership and recovery boundaries.
Case timelines preserve source timestamps and quality/provenance traits; coverage, custody, and export views are deterministic projections of committed case state.
Case holds, retention references, and authorization constrain evidence release and deletion without erasing audit history or invalidating still-referenced exports.
Operators can inspect readiness, collection progress, failures, coverage gaps, and export identity through stable CLI/API and machine-readable outputs; invalid requests do not mutate unrelated state.

The deterministic lab and seed use synthetic metadata and opaque synthetic payloads only, require no real endpoint, account, credential, or external service, and support repeatable normal, partial, failure, restart, and cross-component operation.

APPROVED_WORK_PACKAGE.ENGINEERING_OBJECTIVE: Complete an inherited forensic collection control plane so case-scoped acquisition plans, endpoint/offline collection attempts, immutable evidence manifests, trust decisions, and collection-coverage reporting reconcile correctly through retries and restarts.
APPROVED_WORK_PACKAGE.INHERITED_SYSTEM_STATE: A synthetic but varied estate of endpoint identities, platform capabilities, collection policies, existing case requests, offline collector bundles, prior attempts, artifact metadata, and event/custody history; data-backed scale can naturally use 10,000-20,000 deterministic primary records without real host data or credentials.
APPROVED_WORK_PACKAGE.INSTRUCTION_FIT: PASS: the request can describe case-scoped authorized acquisition, trustworthy provenance, partial-result accounting, restart-safe operation, and deterministic coverage/export in <=20 concise bullets; technical schemas and protocols can remain legitimate operator documentation.
PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: Retrying transport without attempt fencing can let delayed results from an old collection overwrite a newer attempt.
Hashing an item without binding endpoint, case, source, and collection attempt does not establish custody or prevent cross-case reuse.
Counting only successful artifacts hides required sources that are unavailable, partial, rejected, or never attempted.
Persisting collection results but not queue claims/checkpoints can duplicate logical evidence after restart.
Accepting event payload claims without source authority can let untrusted client-originated events impersonate server dispositions.
APPROVED_WORK_PACKAGE.PERSONA: Incident-response evidence custodian coordinating authorized live-endpoint and offline-image collections across a mixed fleet.
PRESERVATION_OBLIGATIONS: Existing case, endpoint, collection, and artifact identifiers remain stable.
Never overwrite prior evidence or rewrite custody history; corrections append a new event.
Unauthorized, stale, malformed, or conflicting collection events fail closed without changing unrelated cases.
Offline evidence remains ingestible without network access and retains its original source identity.
A restart or retry must not lose accepted evidence or create duplicate published items.
APPROVED_WORK_PACKAGE.REASONING_CHAIN: Resolve case and endpoint authority -> validate policy and source compatibility -> schedule an attempt under budget/deadline -> accept only matching trusted attempt events -> reconcile collected bytes and digest/provenance -> reduce partial outcomes -> derive coverage and export from committed custody state.

APPROVED_WORK_PACKAGE.REQUIRED_END_STATE: Operators can submit a case-bound collection plan, see each requested source reach a terminal collected/partial/unavailable/rejected disposition, verify the resulting content and provenance manifest, resume safely after worker or coordinator restart, and export a case package whose reported coverage and custody chain agree with the persisted evidence. No real endpoint, credentials, or external service is needed in grading.
REQUIREMENT_FAMILIES: case and endpoint identity normalization with tenant/case ownership fences

attempt, delivery, and content-digest idempotency with stale-worker fencing
bounded collection budgets, deadlines, and partial/unavailable dispositions
source trust and client/server authority for collection events
immutable item provenance, custody transitions, and append-only audit evidence
restart-safe scheduling, recovery, and exactly-once logical publication
coverage accounting and deterministic case-manifest export
APPROVED_WORK_PACKAGE.SCALE_FIT: PRELIMINARY PASS: a real collection control plane naturally spans case/policy resolution, endpoint capability inventory, planning, scheduling, worker leases, trust/event ingestion, artifact custody, recovery, coverage, and publication. These differentiated responsibilities plausibly support >=3,000 substantive reachable LOC and 20-30 causally related manifestations; A2 must validate the clean architecture can support the scale and 25-30 organic F2P cases before topology or starter work begins.

STATE_MODEL.attempt_and_queue: Every source request has one logical collection item and monotonically numbered attempts. Queue claims and leases are transactional and fenced by worker, attempt, token, and deadline. Retryable transport state is separate from terminal source disposition.
STATE_MODEL.authoritative_store: PostgreSQL is authoritative for case, endpoint inventory generation, policy revision, plans, attempts, leases, result inbox, evidence metadata, custody events, audit, and export jobs.
STATE_MODEL.case_and_policy: Cases have stable case_id, tenant/owner scope, lifecycle, hold state, and monotonic revision. Policy revisions are immutable and plan-bound. Authorization and hold checks precede case rows, counts, artifact metadata, and export reads.
STATE_MODEL.collection_plan: A plan binds case revision, actor, policy revision, endpoint/source identities, source mode (live or offline), requested artifact families, limits, deadlines, and a canonical digest. Submitted plans are immutable; changes create a new plan revision.
STATE_MODEL.coverage_and_timeline: Coverage is derived from requested source dispositions, including complete, partial, unavailable, rejected, cancelled, and failed. Timeline rows retain source time, normalized UTC time, uncertainty/quality traits, and evidence references; projections are rebuildable from committed records.
STATE_MODEL.event_authority: Raw callback bytes are authenticated before parsing. Delivery IDs are unique; identical delivery replay is idempotent and conflicting reuse is rejected. Events bind case, endpoint, collection item, active attempt, source authority, and payload digest.
STATE_MODEL.evidence_and_custody: Synthetic opaque evidence objects are content-addressed. Metadata binds digest, length, case, endpoint, source, plan, item, attempt, capture time, and validation traits. Custody transfers and hold/release decisions append to an immutable ledger; mutable status is a projection.
STATE_MODEL.export_and_retention: Export is a staged job with authorization and hold checks, deterministic ordered manifest, digest verification, atomic publish, and immutable export identity. Retention cannot delete an object while an active case/export reference or hold protects it.
STATE_MODEL.recovery_boundary: Queue claim, attempt/result transition, inbox consumption, custody append, audit, and checkpoint changes commit transactionally around reconcilable lab effects. Restart reclaims expired leases and reconciles lab-visible attempts before reissuing any source action.

UNRESOLVED_RISKS: A3 must avoid turning the architecture into one generic queue/retry defect per test; causal clusters should cross planning, trust, reconciliation, custody, and reporting boundaries.
Need a clear, solver-visible contract for how a synthetic payload digest is computed and how incomplete payload acquisition is represented without implying real-world cryptographic custody.
Define whether timeline ordering uses source time plus uncertainty or only normalized timestamps; requirements must be explicit without overspecifying the implementation.
Confirm the offline container topology remains performant under representative 14,200-record state and that no service requires public-network access during grading.

defects.observable_failure: Two endpoint aliases from different ownership scopes resolve to one canonical key, allowing a collection request to attach to the wrong case owner.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Normalizing only the displayed endpoint name leaves the database identity and authorization lookup inconsistent.

defects.observable_failure: Reusing an idempotency key after policy revision or live/offline source mode changes returns the earlier plan as if its authority were unchanged.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Including requested source names but omitting policy and mode preserves a false idempotency match.

defects.observable_failure: A plan continues to rely on a prior capability generation after endpoint inventory has materially changed, so unsupported acquisition work is scheduled as compatible.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Refreshing inventory for display without binding the plan to its generation leaves execution using stale capability facts.

defects.observable_failure: A case hold or ownership-scope change is not applied to an already-created plan when the plan is later released or exported.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Checking authorization only at plan creation fails to preserve current case authority at later release boundaries.

defects.observable_failure: An unsupported requested source family is dropped from the executable plan but remains absent from the operator-visible requested-source disposition.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Rejecting unsupported sources during execution still leaves the approved plan and coverage denominator misleading.

defects.observable_failure: A per-case evidence budget is enforced separately for each source, allowing a multi-source plan to exceed its aggregate limit.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Per-source limit checks pass individually while the total requested acquisition exceeds the case contract.

defects.observable_failure: Live and offline capture deadlines are normalized differently, so a late offline bundle can be accepted after the equivalent live attempt has expired.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Fixing callback timestamps alone leaves offline intake using a different deadline interpretation.

defects.observable_failure: An explicitly empty source grant is treated like an unspecified grant and expands to the default source set.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Defaulting absent policy fields without preserving the distinction between absent and empty turns a fail-closed policy into broader authority.

defects.observable_failure: A worker renews an expired lease after its attempt has been superseded and continues to act as the owner of current collection work.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Checking the lease token without checking current attempt and deadline does not fence the former worker.

defects.observable_failure: After coordinator restart, the next retry reuses an attempt number that was already issued, making delayed evidence indistinguishable from the new attempt.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Rebuilding queue rows without recovering the monotonic attempt counter preserves a stale-event collision.

defects.observable_failure: A crash between queue claim and attempt ownership commit leaves a claimed item that recovery cannot safely distinguish from undispatched work.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Releasing expired claims alone may repeat a source effect whose dispatch acknowledgement was already accepted.

defects.observable_failure: An ambiguous dispatch acknowledgement is retried as a new collection action rather than reconciled against the existing attempt identity.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Transport retry limits do not prevent duplicate logical collections when the first acknowledgement was lost.

defects.observable_failure: Callback JSON is parsed and fields are trusted before the exact raw-body signature has been verified.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Validating selected envelope fields after parsing does not authenticate the bytes that supplied them.

defects.observable_failure: A previously seen delivery identifier with a different payload is silently treated as an ordinary duplicate.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Delivery-ID deduplication without payload-digest comparison hides event identity conflicts.

defects.observable_failure: A trusted event bound to the case but not to the endpoint, collection item, and active attempt updates the wrong acquisition state.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Case-level authentication does not establish authority for an individual source attempt.

defects.observable_failure: A delayed lower-progress or partial observation regresses a source that was already accepted as complete.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Sorting events by arrival time cannot replace a monotonic state reducer with attempt and observation authority.

defects.observable_failure: A size-limited or interrupted content hash is presented as a complete digest for the evidence item.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Emitting a hash value without an explicit completeness disposition makes partial bytes look verified.

defects.observable_failure: Equal byte digests from separate cases or acquisition sources collapse their metadata into one identity and lose independent provenance.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Content deduplication without preserving case/source references confuses byte identity with evidence identity.

defects.observable_failure: Custody metadata becomes visible before the corresponding evidence object is durable, leaving a committed reference to missing bytes after interruption.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Database transactionality alone cannot make an unflushed object-store write durable.

defects.observable_failure: An untrusted or rejected source event is included in the case timeline even though no evidence item or custody transition was accepted.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Filtering only the final export still exposes rejected observations through ordinary case inspection.

defects.observable_failure: Coverage reports only successful evidence items and omits requested sources that are partial, unavailable, rejected, or never scheduled.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Counting all evidence rows still cannot account for requested sources that produced no row.

defects.observable_failure: The service reports a case ready while accepted inbox events or attempt reconciliations remain pending.
defects.partial_fix_trap: A healthy API process does not establish that durable event and recovery backlogs are drained.

defects.observable_failure: Coverage counts or source facets are computed before case authorization, exposing the existence and volume of another case's evidence.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Filtering visible rows after aggregate calculation still leaks cross-case information.

defects.observable_failure: Equivalent evidence state produces byte-different manifests because item ordering or serialization is not canonical.
defects.partial_fix_trap: Hashing sorted top-level case names does not stabilize nested evidence and custody ordering.

outputs.organic_f2p_surface_assessment: SUFFICIENT, conditional on A2's approved architecture: the six causal clusters generate distinct plan/policy, scheduling/attempt, event-authority, evidence/custody, recovery, and reporting behaviors. The later verifier can derive 25-30 materially distinct F2P cases from these coupled operational surfaces without making one case per defect; A5 must re-evaluate organicity from solver-visible requirements and actual behavior, and the Complexity Governor may return SCENARIO_TOO_SMALL if implementation breadth does not arise naturally.

root_cause_clusters.RC1_IDENTITY_SCOPE_AND_POLICY_BINDING: Case, endpoint, inventory-generation, policy-revision, and plan identities are not consistently bound across plan creation and later intake/release operations.
root_cause_clusters.RC2_PLAN_EXPANSION_AND_BUDGET_SEMANTICS: Source compatibility, explicit policy scope, limits, and deadlines are not compiled into one stable per-case acquisition plan.
root_cause_clusters.RC3_LEASE_ATTEMPT_AND_RESTART_RECOVERY: Queue claims, worker leases, attempt numbering, dispatch acknowledgement, and recovery checkpoints do not share one attempt-fenced lifecycle.
root_cause_clusters.RC4_EVENT_TRUST_AND_MONOTONIC_RECONCILIA: Callback identity, raw-body authority, source/attempt binding, and state reduction are inconsistent under replay, conflict, and delayed observations.
root_cause_clusters.RC5_EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY_AND_CUSTODY_ATOMI: Evidence completeness, source-aware identity, object persistence, custody transitions, and accepted timeline visibility are not consistently committed together.
root_cause_clusters.RC6_COVERAGE_EXPORT_RETENTION_AND_AUTHOR: Coverage, readiness, authorization, retention, and export projections are derived from incomplete or differently scoped state.
